page: Amazon Web Services r5.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance provides 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. This configuration yields 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is not included, meaning the instance relies entirely on network-attached storage, supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core CPU stress tests and memory bandwidth, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 4503.04 GB/sec and uncached large block writes at 98.33 GB/sec. Cryptographic and extended instruction processing are also highly efficient, as shown by strong Passmark CPU encryption scores. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and gzip compression benchmarks falling into the bottom 25%. LLM text generation is also a bottleneck, with the medium 7B model producing only 6.02 tokens per second.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and lack of local storage, the r5.24xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive RAM footprints without the overhead of local NVMe drives. It is well-suited for large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and memory-intensive enterprise applications. The instance is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or GPU-dependent machine learning workloads.
